clue.text: Obliging a fellow with a story

parts.note: a fable is a short moral story

explanation.surface: A helpful chap who comes armed with a tale to tell.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone affable is friendly and easy-going, ready to help, which is what obliging describes.

clue.text: In disbelief, one jumps into swirling Thames

indicators.note: the single letter goes inside the mixed letters, like a diver entering the river
swirling water is churned about, so these letters are mixed up

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone in despair leaps into the churning river in London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is only a link before the definition; 'swirling' scrambles the river's letters and 'jumps into' drops the Roman one inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: Atheism is the lack of belief in any god.

clue.text: Called time with quarter measure

parts.note: a fourth is one quarter
a dimension is a measurement such as length or width

explanation.surface: Last orders called alongside a measure of a quarter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Called time' suggests a pub closing, but it means what time is called in physics.
explanation.definitionFit: In relativity, time is described as the extra coordinate after length, breadth and height.

clue.text: Worker right to be bitter sometimes

parts.note: a worker is a bee in a hive

explanation.surface: An employee is entitled to feel resentful at times.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain bitter is a type of ale, so it is sometimes this.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitter is a British hoppy ale, an example of the drink.

clue.text: Wear out tyre, you might say

definitions.meaning: tyre sounds like tire, meaning to weary

explanation.surface: A tyre becomes worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition goes through a sound-alike: tyre is heard as tire, which means exhaust.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses mean to drain or fatigue: wear out directly, and tire via the sound of tyre.

clue.text: First of history papers put out, possibly

indicators.note: papers that are put out are thrown into disorder, so their letters are rearranged
the opening letter of the next word is all that is taken

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A history paper published first, maybe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' reorders H (from 'First of history') with PAPERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words express uncertainty about whether something is so; they are synonyms.

clue.text: Grassland beyond the river

parts.note: past means beyond, as in past the church
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Grazing land on the far side of the river.
explanation.walkthrough: The URE is a river in North Yorkshire, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Grazing land for cattle and sheep is grass-covered ground.

clue.text: Inspiration for musical pitch?

definitions.meaning: the music style that inspired shows such as ... operas
to sway or toss, as a boat does

explanation.surface: What inspires a musical tone?
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitch' looks like a note's height but means sway, as a ship does.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the popular music genre behind many stage shows; the other is to sway back and forth like a ship.

clue.text: Victor not paid?

parts.note: a winner who competes without a wage, unlike a professional

explanation.surface: A winner who was not given any money.
explanation.definitionFit: A title winner who competes without pay, as opposed to a professional, is this.

clue.text: Italian verse-form, asset in translation?

indicators.note: translating changes a text's form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An Italian poetic form proves valuable once rendered into English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translation' rearranges ASSET plus IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A poem of six six-line stanzas with repeating end-words, originating in Italy and Provence.

clue.text: Noble family doctors?

parts.note: read as the physicians kept by an aristocratic house, which jokingly describes junior hospital doctors who live in

explanation.surface: Medics retained by an aristocratic dynasty.
explanation.walkthrough: A noble family is a house, so its doctors would be its own physicians; really these are hospital doctors resident on site.
explanation.definitionFit: In British hospitals, resident junior doctors on the medical side were given this title.

clue.text: Letter from Greece carried by Cypriot airline

indicators.note: the letters are borne along inside the phrase that follows, as a passenger in a plane

explanation.surface: Post from Athens flown over by a Cyprus airline.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the ninth character of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: People waiting to see gardens here, reportedly

indicators.note: signals that the word must be heard rather than seen on the page

parts.note: Kew Gardens are the famous Royal Botanic Gardens in west London

explanation.surface: Visitors lining up to tour the botanical gardens.
explanation.walkthrough: KEW is the London district home to the Royal Botanic Gardens; it is pronounced the same as the line of people.
explanation.definitionFit: A line of people standing and waiting their turn is the British word for a line.

clue.text: Beautiful fairy looks through one

parts.note: per means through or by means of, as in per post
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A lovely sprite peers through a single opening.
explanation.definitionFit: In Persian mythology this is a graceful, beautiful spirit or elf-like being.

clue.text: He will shortly ring a greeting

parts.note: he will shortened is the contraction he'll
O has the shape of a ring

explanation.surface: He will soon call to say hi.
explanation.definitionFit: A word said when meeting someone, as a salutation.

clue.text: Somebody's opening wine to make merry

indicators.note: the first letter of the word opens it

parts.note: port is a fortified wine from Portugal

explanation.surface: Someone opens a bottle to celebrate.
explanation.definitionFit: To frolic or play is to amuse oneself, to be merry.

clue.text: Central area of America has widest parts around head of Missouri

indicators.note: only the first letter of the state name is used
the word widest is broken into parts and its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A central US region boasts the broadest bits around the upper Missouri.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts' rearranges WIDEST into WIDEST's letters around M from 'head of Missouri', giving MID-WEST.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the name for the north-central region of the United States.

clue.text: Great stores of rope I am to coil

indicators.note: coiling a rope twists it round, so these letters are wound into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Big piles of rope that need winding up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to coil' rearranges ROPE plus I AM.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of a word for a large shop or trading centre, so big stores.

clue.text: Acrobat commonly seen on bars?

definitions.meaning: a gymnast who performs somersaults and falls
a flat-bottomed drinking glass is a frequent sight on pub counters

explanation.surface: A gymnast regularly found on the parallel bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bars' suggests gym apparatus but means pub counters.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a somersaulting performer, the other is a straight-sided drinking glass found in pubs.

clue.text: Large-headed nail can stitch loosely

parts.note: a tin is a can
to tack is to sew with long loose temporary stitches

explanation.surface: A big nail that can loosely hold sewing.
explanation.definitionFit: A short nail with a broad flat head, coated in tin.

clue.text: Bread to soak up pickled herring

parts.note: a roll is a bread item
to mop is to wipe up liquid

explanation.surface: Using a bread roll to mop up the herring.
explanation.definitionFit: A rolled fillet of herring pickled in vinegar.

clue.text: Crossbred dog inelegant on the move?

definitions.meaning: a cross between a greyhound and a collie or terrier, used by poachers
someone who staggers or lurches as they go along

explanation.surface: A mongrel hound that moves clumsily.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a type of crossbred dog; the other is one who lurches, staggering awkwardly while moving.

clue.text: Pasta dish to droop in the country way

indicators.note: the droop word goes inside the country road

parts.note: a lane is a narrow rural road
to sag is to droop

explanation.surface: A pasta dish wilting in a rural style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'country way' looks like 'rustic manner' but means a lane.
explanation.definitionFit: Baked layers of flat pasta, sauce and cheese.

clue.text: Amount of money in grass picked up again…

indicators.note: the money word sits inside the grass

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass
a sum is an amount of money

explanation.surface: Money hidden in the grass is picked up once more.
explanation.definitionFit: To resume is to take up again after a break.

clue.text: Fix no starting-time for office to open

definitions.text: Fix no starting-time for office to open

parts.words: Fix no starting-time for office to open
parts.note: read as asking for the number (no.) fixed as the usual hour when office work begins

explanation.surface: An instruction not to set a time for opening the office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' looks like a negative but is the abbreviation for number: the number fixed as the office's starting hour.
explanation.definitionFit: Nine o'clock is the traditional hour at which an office day begins.

clue.text: Additional little husband is costly

parts.note: plus means additional, as in a plus factor
H is the short form of husband in records and lists

explanation.surface: An extra small spouse proves expensive.
explanation.definitionFit: Plush means luxurious and expensive-looking, so dear or costly.

clue.text: A doctor's making a profit, would you say?

definitions.note: spoken aloud, profit is heard as prophet

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor; with the 's it gives the letters MOS

explanation.surface: A medic is turning a profit.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a sound pun: 'a profit' said aloud is 'a prophet', an Old Testament one.
explanation.definitionFit: He was an Old Testament prophet with a book of the Bible named after him.

clue.text: … extra for rent?

definitions.meaning: spare or surplus, in British slang

explanation.surface: Extra money paid for the rent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' is not a payment but a tear.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is British slang for spare or surplus; the other is a long deep cut or tear.

clue.text: The Secret Life of Walter Mitty

indicators.note: something secret is concealed, so the letters lie tucked away in the name

explanation.surface: The title of a well-known short story and film about a daydreamer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Life' is a prison sentence, which is a period of imprisonment.
explanation.definitionFit: A life sentence is a period served in prison, a fixed spell of time.

clue.text: Attractive quality of polar bears, for example

definitions.meaning: personal charm or allure that draws people
creatures of the poles, taken whimsically as magnets

explanation.surface: Polar bears have a certain charm.
explanation.walkthrough: Polar bears live near the magnetic poles, so as animals they can be said to have magnetism.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means personal sexual or charismatic allure, and literally beasts with magnetism.

clue.text: Bond displaying his pink form?

indicators.note: putting the letters into a new form means rearranging them

explanation.surface: Showing the pink bond of a fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' rearranges HIS PINK.
explanation.definitionFit: Family relationship is a bond or tie between relatives.

clue.text: Sovereign dug up? Looks like a noble!

parts.note: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, a queen
mined means extracted by digging

explanation.surface: A monarch unearthed appears aristocratic.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the queen's cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: Peers' ceremonial robes are trimmed with white stoat fur, so wearing it marks nobility.
